basis: S2-sync measured 10 KiB same-stream all-reduce 8.32/8.39 us per step; S1 link and S2 collectives same box. Per-layer GEMV byte cost estimated from 8704x5120 bf16 = 89.1 MB at the box's 1701 GB/s wall, i.e. an ESTIMATE, not measured throughput.
question: Does a 64-layer chain of real-shaped GEMV + 10 KiB all-reduce + RMSNorm capture in one graph per card, replay correctly, and reproduce the sum of its separately measured parts?
correctness: Identical weights and inputs on both ranks, so the SUM all-reduce is an exact doubling. Two independent checks: (1) a graph replay is compared against a no-collective reference chain that substitutes the exact factor 2, requiring bit equality and recording max abs difference; (2) the comm-only chain starts at pattern*2^-64 and must end exactly at pattern after 64 doublings.

criteria.S4_graphs_3x_eager: toy chain only; expected to be at risk because the 10 KiB collective is a large share of per-layer GPU time
criteria.M0_projection_reproduction: shard chain per-pass time versus measured compute-only plus comm-only

scope: bf16 weights, not the production int4 Marlin kernel; no model, no attention, no KV cache. Native same-stream NCCL only; ProcessGroup parity was established in S2-sync at the collective level. Two complete runs, forward and reverse variant order, then decide once.
